title: Word Break (DP)
description: Bottom-up DP: dp[i] is true iff s[0..i] can be segmented into dictionary words. Transition: dp[i] = ∃ j < i with dp[j] true AND s[j..i] in the dict.

notes: dp[0] = true is the base case — the empty prefix is trivially segmentable.
Inner loop j scans 0..i-1: j marks the END of the previous word and the START of the candidate s[j..i].
Break as soon as you set dp[i] = true — one valid split suffices.

options: Whether s[0..i] can be segmented into dictionary words
Longest dict word at index i
Empty prefix is segmentable, letting dp[i] turn on when s[0..i] is itself a word
Off-by-one fix in the loop bounds
It is wrong — should be false

questions.q: Why use a Set for wordDict instead of an array?
options: O(1) average membership check vs O(d) for array.includes

exercises.prompt: Fill in the bottom-up DP. dp[i] is true if some split point j makes dp[j] true AND s.slice(j, i) is in the dict.

blanks.hint: candidate word is s[j..i) — endpoint is i

L3.prompt: Write `wordBreak(s, wordDict)` using bottom-up DP. Log `wordBreak("applepenapple", ["apple","pen"])` then `wordBreak("catsandog", ["cats","dog","sand","and","cat"])`.
hints: dp length is s.length + 1; dp[0] = true.
Outer i: end of the prefix. Inner j: split point — check dp[j] AND s.slice(j, i) is a dict word.
"catsandog" fails: no split of the suffix "og" is in the dict.
